comment: Great guy, keeps class entertaining! There was a lot of writing for sure, but he gives feedback on each one so it is easy to improve.

super sweet guy and easy class. its fun and you learn a bit about different cultures which is cool. he brings in people from around the world to teach you about new instruments and how to play them, and there's a performance at the end that you participate in but its genuinely so chill. id take this class for a gen ed for sure.
Just go to the rehersal and u would earn a A
If you attend all classes, you get an A. Gamlean is a good thing to explore.
One of the best professors at UR. Course material is extremely interesting and hands on, a lot of time is spent playing music and interacting with the community. Would recommend to basically anyone.

This professor has been my favorite to work with. He is always really clear on his expectations of students, and gives enough time to complete assignments. The classes are engaging and fun, and he makes sure all students participate. Dr. McGraw is a professor I would recommend to everyone! This is my favorite class of all time.

Andy is one of the most fun, passionate, and hilarious professors I've had. He brings in guest speakers/performers from all different cultures, which is super interesting. You will have to read articles and write 200 words before most classes, and attend concerts outside of class which is kind of annoying. But overall I really enjoyed this class!

Andy's feedback is helpful on papers (sends a detailed voice memo with feedback & will read your drafts before you submit them). He intersperses discussions on academic articles with percussion practice on world instruments. He can sometimes be unclear on assignments but just ask for clarification. A few projects/concerts are outside of class time.

Dr McGraw's rubrics are a couple of sentences long and offer zero guidance, but he will then take off points for you not doing things that are not listed in the rubric. Get ready for no help or instructions whatsoever and penalties for missing things you were never told to do. Worst professor ever for the single dumbest class I have ever taken.

This class (Anthropology of Music) was an interesting class, but be ready for big papers! Dr. McGraw is good about giving you time to do things, but DONT FALL BEHIND ON YOUR PROJECTS! Stay ahead of it and you will be fine. He is very funny and knowledgeable, but the class has a few projects that take a lot of time. Dr. McGraw is a great professor.
No grades until the last day of class. No substance. Final project has little to do with anything discussed in class.
Not a very understanding guy, could've been more clear, didn't realize that not everyone is proficient in percussive instruments and that there is a steep learning curve, a little full of himself.

Andy is very invested in these musics and wants you to be too. This class is fun, but don't take it as an "easy" class unless you're used to being a musician. Andy travels a lot and has great stories. Super funny and easy to get help from.

Andy is brilliant and a lot of fun. As a music major, this was an easy class. Disclaimer for non-majors: you have to practice the music, and there are papers. Heavy group work.   Ladies: if you have male group members who are slacking off, tell Andy. He will not let them get away with making you do all the work. Very caring if you are frustrated.

Interesting experience. Meeting native performers and working with authentic instruments is truly cool. However, the course is way more time-consuming than you expect and he sometimes forgets we're not music majors. Andy's also a bit of a B-grader and the writing prompts (including  3 relatively time-consuming essays) need to be clearer.

He expects too much from students. Heavy reading load, field trips on less than a week's notice with no transportation provided. He changed our final project (included 10 page paper) due date less than a week beforehand to four days earlier. Class is not accessible at all to those taking it for music credit. Treated as 300 level anth class. Avoid.

I took "What Does Sound Say" with McGraw this semester and really enjoyed my time in the class. At the beginning of the course, McGraw catered the syllabus to what the class wanted to learn throughout the semester which I thought was really cool. You have to do the readings in order to be able to contribute anything meaningful to the discussions

I found Prof McGraw's teaching to be engaging & inspired. He packages the material in fun, innovative ways, e.g. played Guitar Hero & asmt submission via blog. Indeed, he demands a high level of understanding for top marks; however it's not impossible (myself being proof). He appreciates intellectual curiosity; be involved, ask Qs & you'll be fine.

The problem: ethnomusicology is the least accessible subfield in music scholarship, and he will grade you on your understanding not your effort level. The material is difficult and can only be simplified so much. Be prepared for some music theory, philosophy, anthropology, psychology. If you like these and like studying you'll have a ball with Andy
He's a total B grader and doesn't explain well what he wants for assignments. Nothing is enough for him as he's trying to prove he is really smart in order to get tenure.
very into what he is teaching.  lots of boring reading assignments.
